#COLANOW
Why New Jersey Retirees Need COLA Now
The restoration of a Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) for New Jersey’s retired police officers, firefighters, teachers, and other public employees is fundamentally an issue of retirement security, fairness, and the preservation of earned benefits.
For decades, public employees dedicated their careers to serving the residents of New Jersey. Police officers and firefighters accepted the risks and demands of public safety service. Teachers devoted their professional lives to educating future generations. Throughout their careers, these employees made mandatory contributions to their pension systems with the expectation that the retirement benefits they earned would provide a stable and secure income throughout retirement.
However, the prolonged suspension of COLA has resulted in a significant erosion of pension purchasing power. While pension benefit amounts have remained largely unchanged, the cost of essential goods and services has increased substantially. Retirees now face dramatically higher expenses for healthcare, prescription medications, property taxes, housing, utilities, insurance, transportation, and everyday necessities. As a result, many retirees are forced to maintain the same standard of living with retirement incomes that effectively buy less each year.
A pension benefit that remains fixed during periods of inflation does not maintain its value. In practical terms, the absence of COLA functions as a reduction in real income. Each year inflation increases while pension benefits remain unchanged, retirees experience a decline in purchasing power. For individuals who have been retired for many years, this cumulative loss can amount to thousands of dollars annually and substantially diminish the financial security they worked a lifetime to achieve.
The issue is particularly significant for public-sector retirees because, unlike active employees, they generally do not have opportunities to offset inflation through wage increases, promotions, or overtime. Most retirees rely primarily on their pension and Social Security benefits. As inflation continues to rise, the financial burden falls disproportionately on those living on fixed incomes.
The restoration of COLA should not be viewed as the creation of a new benefit. Rather, it is a mechanism designed to preserve the value of benefits that have already been earned through years of public service and employee contributions. The purpose of a COLA is to ensure that retirement benefits retain their intended value over time and continue to provide the level of retirement security originally contemplated when employees entered public service.
Furthermore, restoring COLA would provide broader economic benefits to New Jersey communities. Retirees spend their income locally on housing, healthcare, food, transportation, and other essential goods and services. Maintaining the purchasing power of pension benefits helps support local businesses, strengthens communities, and contributes to economic stability throughout the state.
The question before New Jersey is not simply a fiscal one. It is a question of honoring commitments made to generations of public servants who dedicated their careers to protecting lives, educating children, and serving the public interest. Retirement security should not diminish solely because inflation increases over time. A pension that steadily loses value year after year undermines the purpose of the retirement system itself.
Restoring COLA would help ensure that New Jersey’s retired police officers, firefighters, teachers, and public employees can maintain the dignity, financial stability, and quality of life they earned through decades of dedicated service. It represents a commitment to fairness, fiscal responsibility, and the principle that earned retirement benefits should retain their value throughout retirement.
Honor the commitment to public servants, do the right thing!
NJ Retired
